To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the deletion of two major chuperone proteins in yeast, SSA1 and SSA1, results in an overall increase of protein abundance, (ii) this increase is not reflected in individual proteins and is not due to paralogous proteins, (iii) the robustness to loss of these major hubs can be explained by the overall network structure, and (iv) the robustness is a consequence of the folding workload of the network.
The loss of major hub proteins in the HSP70 network of S. cerevisiae is tolerated by a compensatory increase in protein abundance, but this is not a consequence of paralogous proteins.

the HSP70 network is robust to the loss of major chaperones, and that this robustness cannot simply be explained by the presence or absence of paralogues, but instead is a consequence of the overall network topology.

the robustness of the HSP70 network, which is an important feature in the maintenance of protein homeostasis.
the role of the major chaperones SSA1 and Ssb1 in the chaperone Hsp70 network.

the robustness of the network is a result of a combination of the overall network architecture and the presence of paralogs, but that the presence of parologs alone does not explain the observed robustness.
the robustness of the HSP70 network to deletion of major hub proteins is a product of network topology and the overall folding workload.
the robustness of the chaperone networks in yeast is a product of its overall structure.

the HSP70 network is highly robust to the loss of major hub nodes.
